<div class="main">

<div class="prose">
<span class="kicker">About</span>
<p>I am an Associate Research Scientist (Research faculty) in the <a href="https://ysph.yale.edu/public-health-research-and-practice/department-research/biostatistics/">Department of Biostatistics</a> at the <a href="https://ysph.yale.edu/">Yale School of Public Health</a>, working with <a href="https://ysph.yale.edu/profile/bhramar-mukherjee/">Dr. Bhramar Mukherjee</a>. My work bridges <span class="hl-ehr">EHR-derived real-world evidence</span> and <span class="hl-dose">early-phase drug development</span>, with methodological contributions in causal inference, survival and longitudinal data analysis, covariate adjustment, and Bayesian dose optimization.</p>
<p>My first-author methodology has appeared in <em>Biometrika</em>, the <em>Annals of Applied Statistics</em>, and <em>Statistics in Medicine</em>, with related work revised and resubmitted at the <em>Journal of the American Statistical Association</em> and <em>Biometrics</em>. My current EHR research spans <em>All of Us</em>, the UK Biobank, Yale New Haven Health, the Michigan Genomics Initiative, and Epic Cosmos.</p>
</div>

<div class="focus">
<span class="kicker">Research focus</span>
<div class="themes">
<div class="theme a1">
<h3 class="anchored">Methods for Electronic Health Records</h3>
<p>Joint models that correct the biases from informative visiting and observation in large-scale EHR data.</p>
</div>
<div class="theme a2">
<h3 class="anchored">Adaptive Dose-Finding Design</h3>
<p>Seamless phase I–II designs that use biological mediators and survival endpoints to optimize dose.</p>
</div>
<div class="theme a3">
<h3 class="anchored">Clinical Trial Methodology</h3>
<p>Meta-analytic and covariate-adjusted methods that sharpen inference across early-phase trials.</p>
</div>
<div class="theme a4">
<h3 class="anchored">Optimal Treatment Regime</h3>
<p>Model-free variable screening for individualized treatment decisions in high-dimensional survival data.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>

</div>
